data.gender_notes: Leola is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Leola is derived from the Greek word 'leos' meaning 'lion' and 'ola' meaning 'little shepherdess'. This name was often given to girls in ancient Greece who were believed to have the strength and courage of a lion and the nurturing and protective qualities of a shepherdess. The name Leola carries the meaning “Little shepherdess” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Leola usually hope their child will grow to embody little shepherdess and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The name Leola has been popularized through various medieval legends and folktales. In one such tale, a young shepherdess named Leola is known for her exceptional courage and strength, ensuring the safety of her flock against any harm that may come their way. This narrative reinforces the value of bravery and the importance of taking care of others, making the name Leola a symbol of empowerment and resilience in various cultures.
data.spiritual_significance: Leola is also a name with deep spiritual significance, often associated with the biblical figures of Leah, a beloved wife of Jacob, and Rachel, Jacob’s other wife. Leah was given the name 'Leah' meaning 'weary' due to her laborious childbearing. Rachel was originally called 'Rachel' meaning 'ewe' because she was the one who was more industrious and tended the flock. In this context, the name Leola implies the spiritual strength and endurance inherent in the biblical matriarchs Leah and Rachel. It also underscores the eternal nurturing and protective role of a shepherdess in caring for her flock – a metaphor for the divine love and care of our Creator towards humanity.
